plan.title: Mouse tumor immune/stromal composition: anti-PD-1 vs isotype
plan.analytical_narrative:
The question asks for the immune and stromal composition of each of the 12 subcutaneous tumors (6 anti-PD-1, 6 isotype control) and whether composition differs between arms. The input is a single gene-level count matrix from Salmon (12000 genes x 12 samples, mouse gene symbols) plus a 12 x 2 metadata table with a condition column; the design is unpaired, single batch, no covariates. Sample sample_01 has a library size about 4x below the median, so QC keeps and inspects it rather than dropping it silently (R-0008), and depth is handled by size factors rather than by exclusion (R-0030).

The knowledge service flagged the deconvolution step: human reference methods (MCP-counter, xCell, EPIC, quanTIseq) must not be run on mouse data (R-0136), and the mouse tool of record is mMCP-counter. A package check confirms mMCPcounter 1.1.0 IS installed in this environment, so the flag's condition ('absent from this pool') does not hold here and the step proceeds with the mouse tool; the human methods listed in `forbids` are excluded. mMCP-counter is a marker-based abundance score, not a fraction, so results are reported as relative abundance per cell population, comparable across samples within a population and NOT across populations.

Structure: T1 does QC/filtering/normalization on the counts and produces both the linear-scale CPM matrix that deconvolution requires (R-0129) and a log-CPM matrix for rank-based scoring. T3S2 runs mMCP-counter for the composition estimate. T3S1 runs UCell scores on independent mouse marker sets as an orthogonal check on the same populations, since a single marker-based method on 12000 genes can miss populations whose markers were filtered out. T3S3 tests every population score between arms with limma under the same two-group design, BH-adjusted across populations, and reports effect sizes with confidence intervals — with 6 vs 6 mice this is a small study and the test is powered only for large composition shifts, which the report must state. T1S3 assembles the per-sample composition table, the between-arm comparison, and the reproducibility record.

The import state of the Salmon counts is unknown (no statement of length correction), so CPM rather than TPM is the deconvolution input and that choice is stated with the result. No differential expression on genes is planned: the question stops at composition, and an unasked gene-level DE would be scope the user did not request. Composition here is the outcome, not a covariate (R-0132).

steps.name: Anti-PD-1 vs isotype comparison of composition scores
steps.question: Does any immune or stromal population differ in abundance between the 6 anti-PD-1 and the 6 isotype control tumors?
steps.description: Take the mMCP-counter population scores (T3S2) and the UCell signature scores (T3S1) as two score matrices, each population/signature x 12 samples. For each matrix, fit limma with the same two-group design used throughout (~condition, anti-PD-1 vs isotype control as named in the metadata, no covariates, unpaired) — the unit of the test is the 6+6 mice, not the genes. Adjust p-values with Benjamini-Hochberg ACROSS the populations tested within each matrix, reporting the number tested. Report per population: group means, the difference with a 95% confidence interval, the raw and BH-adjusted p-value, and a per-sample dot/box plot with sample_01 marked. Also report the Spearman concordance between the mMCP-counter score and the corresponding UCell signature for each population that both cover. State plainly that 6 vs 6 mice gives power only for large composition shifts, that a non-significant population is not evidence of no change, and that both score types are relative — a shift can arise from a change in another compartment (e.g. tumor cellularity) rather than from a true change in the population itself.
steps.context: Composition is the outcome of this analysis, not a covariate in a gene-level model; no gene-level differential expression is planned because the research question stops at composition.
acceptance_criteria: limma fitted on the score matrices with the two-group design using the actual condition level names, one test per population/signature
BH adjustment applied across populations within each score matrix, with the number of tests reported
A results table gives group means, difference with 95% CI, raw p and BH-adjusted p per population
Per-sample visualizations show all 12 points with sample_01 identifiable
Concordance between mMCP-counter and UCell is reported for overlapping populations
The report states the power limitation of 6 vs 6 and that null results are not evidence of absence
constraints: signature_scoring: score_test = limma on the scores with the design
signature_scoring: score_adjustment = BH across signatures
The test unit is the 12 mice; do not treat genes as replicates
Do not use composition scores as a covariate in any gene-level model in this plan — they are the outcome here
caveats: Marker-based scores of different populations are on different arbitrary scales; only within-population between-group comparisons are meaningful
Anti-PD-1 treatment can change marker gene expression per cell (e.g. activation markers) independently of cell number, so a score shift is not proof of a change in cell abundance
With n=6 per arm, one influential animal can drive a nominally significant result — inspect the per-sample plots before interpreting

grounding.reason: Per-sample composition scores compared between two groups: limma on the score matrix under the study design with BH across signatures per R-0134@0f16; composition treated as the outcome per R-0132@246d.

steps.name: Composition report and reproducibility record
steps.question: What is the per-sample immune and stromal composition of the 12 mouse tumors, and which populations differ between anti-PD-1 and isotype control?
steps.description: Assemble the final report: (1) the per-sample composition table — every sample as a row, every mMCP-counter population and UCell signature as a column, with the condition label; (2) a heatmap of composition scores across the 12 samples, samples annotated by arm; (3) the between-arm comparison table from T3S3 with effect sizes, confidence intervals and BH-adjusted p-values; (4) a methods statement recording that mMCP-counter (mouse) was used and that human-reference deconvolution methods were excluded because the samples are mouse, that input was linear CPM (not TPM, because the Salmon length-correction state is unrecorded), that scores are relative abundances and not fractions, that sample_01 was retained despite its ~4x-below-median library size and how it behaved in QC and in the composition scores, and that with 6 vs 6 mice only large composition differences are detectable. Include the reproducibility record: sessionInfo, random seeds, package versions, and the version of every marker/gene-set collection used.
steps.context: Final deliverable answering both halves of the research question: composition of every sample, and whether it differs between arms.
acceptance_criteria: A per-sample composition table covering all 12 samples with condition labels is delivered
A composition heatmap annotated by treatment arm is produced
The between-arm results table with effect sizes, CIs and adjusted p-values is included
The methods statement records the mouse-only method choice, the CPM input rationale, the relative-score caveat, sample_01's handling, and the power limitation
Reproducibility record includes sessionInfo, seeds, package versions, and marker collection versions
constraints: report: reproducibility_record = session_info, seed, package_versions, collection_version, annotation_release
Do not present marker-based scores as cell fractions or percentages anywhere in the report
Do not claim a treatment effect for any population whose BH-adjusted p-value does not support it
caveats: The report must not extrapolate from a 12-sample mouse experiment to human anti-PD-1 biology

grounding.reason: No rule covers the report step itself; the reproducibility record follows R-0086@becf.

flags.message: If one sample has a library size several times below the median of the study, do not delete it in silence. Keep it through the sample structure QC, look at it on the PCA and on the sample distance heatmap, report its library size and its detected genes beside the others, and remove it only with a stated reason. The count models down-weight a low-depth sample through its size factor, thus removal is a judgment, not a default.

Do not run a human deconvolution method on mouse data. The marker sets and the reference profiles of MCP-counter, xCell, EPIC, and quanTIseq come from human samples, and a mouse symbol that maps to a human marker does not carry the same specificity in mouse tissue. The mouse tool of record is mMCP-counter, the mouse version of MCP-counter with markers from mouse data, and it is absent from this pool. Stop the deconvolution and ask for mMCP-counter or for a mouse reference, or give a descriptive signature score from mouse marker sets with the caution that it is not a deconvolution.
